A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HSRDM research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original FigureEight simulations, quantitative NBA forecasting experiments, and analysis of eight soldiers' heading trajectories.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical studies and adds original MarchingBand simulations with quantitative system-state segmentation results.

M1.justification: The two-level latent hierarchy, recurrent transition models, autoregressive emissions, variational updates and partial forecasting procedure are retained in Sections 2–3 and Appendices B–C. MarchingBand instantiates the existing framework with task-specific settings.

E1.justification: V2 adds MarchingBand: ten simulated sequences involving 64 entities, with letter formations and collective reset events used to evaluate system-state recovery. This substantially expands the tested coordination scenarios. FigureEight, basketball and soldier data are retained.

E2.justification: GroupNet becomes an evaluated NBA forecasting comparator in v2 Table 1 and Figure 3; v1 only cited it in related work. Its inclusion materially strengthens the comparison because it outperforms HSRDM in the reported forecasting errors. The existing NBA comparators remain.

E3.justification: FigureEight DSARF changes from five to two discrete states, with strategy-specific lag/factor searches and MSE-based selection replacing the earlier shared settings and ELBO-based selection. Forecast samples increase from three to five. MarchingBand introduces clustering and state-alignment procedures. NBA forecasting is described for all ten players in v1 but explicitly for five Cavaliers starters in v2, limiting direct score comparability.

E4.justification: V2 adds MarchingBand ablations testing system states and recurrence, plus analysis of FigureEight forecast consistency across initializations. It removes the FigureEight learned-segmentation and distance-conditioned transition-matrix diagnostics in v1 Figures D.6 and D.8. The NBA ablation analyses remain.

E5.justification: FigureEight DSARF runs explicitly increase from four to ten, while five HSRDM/rAR-HMM initializations are newly specified. V2 adds forecast-MSE standard errors, across-trial medians and MarchingBand best/median accuracies, and documents excluded outliers and replacement of failed runs. NBA diagnostic testing changes from a stated 0.01 threshold to 0.05.

E6.justification: V2 adds FigureEight MSE results and MarchingBand accuracies: HSRDM achieves 88% best and 83% median, versus 80%/69% without recurrence, 48%/42% for rAR-HMM and 38%/32% for DSARF. NBA HSRDM's 20-game error changes from 14.4 to 13.4 feet, with newly evaluated GroupNet at 12.4 feet; HSRDM's in-bounds rate changes from 0.915 to 0.954. These are revised reports whose differing evaluation descriptions prevent a simple matched-setting improvement claim.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B.5 revise the likelihood-bound formulation to condition on parameters and distinguish it from the prior-augmented objective. V1's Appendix A.3 entropy derivation is replaced by a reference to Hughes et al. (2015). The principal filtering, smoothing and variational-inference derivations remain.

C1.justification: The hierarchy, recurrence and linear-in-entities inference contributions remain central. The abstract and introduction recalibrate forecasting claims toward competitive accuracy with substantially smaller, cheaper models, and make comparative hidden-state recovery an explicit empirical claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of GroupNet's accuracy versus HSRDM's resource costs, initialization-dependent forecasting reliability, and MarchingBand's fixed-duration model misspecification. It removes v1 Appendix F.4's detailed basketball discussion of boundary handling, richer covariates and higher-order recurrence. General scalability and expressivity limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility information through FigureEight iteration and M-step budgets, DSARF search grids and selected settings, MarchingBand generation/training details, and the soldier experiment's iteration count. The reported code repository changes from dynagroup to team-dynamics-time-series. Many basketball settings are retained or relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: V2 adds a comparison with Brenner et al.'s hierarchical RNN work and citations to Babadi, Odden and Russ, Hughes, and Munkres. The Wojnowicz et al. (2023) citation disappears with the basketball future-work discussion. The broader positioning against switching-state, personalized and multi-agent models remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten, with experiments organized into task-specific goals, baseline selection, configuration, training and results. The title changes from 'synchronous' to 'coordinated,' author information changes, and the appendices are reorganized.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Figure 2 is redesigned around forecast overlays and an MSE table; NBA tables become paired subtables and Figure 3 gains a GroupNet row. MarchingBand adds a figure and table, while the old FigureEight appendix plots disappear. The soldier figure is retained and rearranged.

improvement.justification: V1 supported system-state discovery mainly through qualitative examples. V2 substantially strengthens this central contribution with a 64-entity segmentation experiment, ablations and across-trial summaries. Quantified FigureEight forecasting and the stronger GroupNet comparison also support more carefully calibrated accuracy/resource claims. These gains outweigh the loss of some appendix diagnostics, although inconsistent Independent versus Concatenation descriptions for MarchingBand DSARF and ambiguity around revised NBA scoring still limit reproducibility.
